judged_text: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71) but the guest email is compared raw (line 77) and the existing-attendee check uses === on raw strings (line 76), so neither comparison is case-normalized. A blacklisted address submitted as 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and receives the invite, and re-adding an existing attendee with different letter case creates a second Attendee row so that person is emailed twice and appears twice on the calendar event.

A blacklisted address submitted as 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and receives the invite, and re-adding an existing attendee with different letter case creates a second Attendee row so that person is emailed twice and appears twice on the calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (`split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but `uniqueGuests` filters with `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` using the raw `guest` string from input, so mixed-case submissions can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, the duplicate check `!booking.attendees.some(attendee => guest === attendee.email)` is a raw string equality check, so `Spam@X.com` vs `spam@x.com` would not be detected as an existing attendee and could be inserted via `createMany`, resulting in duplicate attendee rows/emails.
